text:
B: Hey, hey! Alright? Callum.
A: Alright, mate. Darren.
B: Darren, nice one. Love the polo, very official. Are you on your lunch or finished?
A: Finished. Just got in. What're we meant to be talking about, d'you know?
B: No idea, mate, just chatting, I think. I just had a girl from Basingstoke, Gemma, she was nice. Bit scary.
A: I'm Basingstoke. Brighton Hill.
B: No way! You lot are everywhere. Is it all car sales down there? She was car sales. I'm car sales.
A: Builders' merchant. I run a branch. Yard, trade counter, deliveries.
B: Oh, proper. So like timber, bricks, all that?
A: Timber, aggregates, plasterboard, the lot. Had a delivery two hours late this morning and half the town's builders stood in my yard moaning at me, so. Not the best start.
B: Two hours! What do you even do with them?
A: Tell the driver what I think of him. Then deal with the lads. It's not complicated, it just shouldn't happen.
B: Ha, I bet. We get that with transporters, car turns up a day late and the customer thinks I've done it on purpose. I'm in Stevenage, by the way, used and nearly-new.
A: Right. Saturdays?
B: Six days, mate. Saturdays are the worst, I'm knackered by the Sunday.
A: Same, I do every other one. Who d'you support, then? You've got an Arsenal mug there.
B: You clocked it! Yeah, Arsenal, through my dad. You?
A: Reading.
B: Oh. Erm. Sorry.
A: Yeah, don't. Lost again Saturday. The owners haven't got a clue, the manager's out of his depth, and every year we're told it's a rebuild. I used to have a season ticket. Now I just go a few times a year with my lad.
B: How old's your lad?
A: Nine. Alfie. He's with his mum mostly, so I take him when I've got him. He loves it, even when they're rubbish.
B: That's nice, though. That's what it's about, innit. Ha, sorry, I don't know why I said innit. My dad used to take me to the Emirates, still does sometimes, if someone's got a spare.
A: Yeah. It's good to have that. Erm, yeah. So, cars. Do you ever get deals or is that a myth?
B: Ha, it depends who's asking, mate. For you, I'd be honest.
A: Would you?
B: Mostly! No, I would. Honestly, finance on used, it's all in the APR. People look at the monthly and not the total. That's the bit you want to watch.
A: That's what I thought. I've got a car loan now, I'm not looking at it too hard.
B: Yeah, you and me both, mate. Mine's a bit much, if I'm honest. Erm, what do you do to switch off, then? Gym? You look like a gym man.
A: Three mornings a week, weights. My dad had a heart attack at fifty-eight, so.
B: Oh, mate, sorry. Is he okay?
A: He's alright now. Watches what he eats, sort of. Friday's still a curry, mind.
B: Got to keep Friday. I've been doing padel, way harder than it looks, you'd—
